owner: SharedRoom rank 607 (room and its seats under one row lock); families project wire shapes; Combat keeps attempts and rosters
clauses: C1 One owner of membership, seats, ready, lifecycle, lease, state_version and notice_version. Family-specific data stays in a family payload; the core has no family branches.

C2 Lock order: actor fence, I4 player roots ascending for every member touched, family 605 rows, occurrence 606, room 607, Combat 609, I5 610+. Read the room unlocked to learn members, lock, then recheck state_version and retry through the abort budget (8 attempts, 20-80 ms).
C3 One active room per player per family slot, enforced by a partial unique index. Capacity, level band and throttle are refused server side; the client's checks are UI only.
C4 Numeric wire room_id, 0 means no room. Owner leave, expiry and last leave close the room idempotently; closed rooms never reopen; kicked players cannot rejoin that room.

C5 combat.Rooms.AdmitTx is the production binding: the roster must equal the seated members of the convener's open room in seat order, all ready, status not closed. It runs inside START, and a replayed START never calls it.
C6 Team fights are one attempt with one terminal and SettleMemberTx per member; value grants through I5 keyed by member receipt (D24). A reconnect never restarts a terminal fight.
C7 Pushes are best effort: pg_notify wakeup inside the transaction, realtime reloads and projects. Every family has a read MID which is authoritative, so a lost push cannot strand a client.
C8 Reconcile loop closes expired rooms in bounded batches and is safe beside live commands.
C9 No client value is stored as authority: partner ids are checked against owned heroes, duplicates and foreign pets refused.
